newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Weighed down by fresh supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Weighed down by fresh supplies.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices extended their three-month long price slide for another week on pressures of new supplies amid poor demand from gasoline blenders, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The market is still under pressure despite some new demand from Taiwan because of excess supplies," one trader said.
Free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting in May was assessed between $255 and $260 per tonne, down from $260-$265 last week.

The weak market was clearly reflected in the Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) latest tender to buy 3,500 tonnes of MTBE which was awarded at between $8-$13 per tonne below the previous purchase.
CPC awarded the tender for June 10-24 delivery at around $267 per tonne cost-and-freight Taiwan, well below its May 6-20 purchase at between $275 to $280 per tonne.

Traders said new supplies are entering the market following the start up of a 50,000 tonne-per-year plant in Singapore as part of the Singapore $3.4 billion petrochemical complex which started producing on specification ethylene early last week.
In addition to the Singapore plant, the 700,000 tonne per year Sadaf plant in Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia, is expected to begin commercial production next month, traders said.
Traders said there were suggestions earlier that the plant, a joint-venture between Saudi Basic Industries Corp and Royal Dutch Shell, might start up as late as July.
Traders said as a result of these additional supplies, the Malaysian producer who operates a MTBE/propylene plant is maximising propylene output, traders said.
On the demand side, traders said, despite the large unleaded gasoline award by CPC last week, there are not that much more incremental demand especially from Singapore blenders.
CPC bought three 250,000-barrel 95-octane unleaded reformate for May 16-31 and June 1-15 arrival at $24.60-24.70 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan.
Gasoline blenders say the lower demand are partly due to the poor octane spread which for between 97 and 95 octane is at about 50 cents.
As a result it is not very lucrative to blend up the gasoline with the more expensive MTBE unless it is mandated in the consumer country, they said.
